issues.detail: Error handling is documented in guidelines but missing from Instructions and Examples (file not found, missing columns, invalid data types, permission errors).

scenarios.name: deduplicate-and-export
scenarios.rationale: Response A covers all rubric requirements explicitly: it loads CSV with pd.read_csv(), prints shape (rows × columns) and column names immediately, uses drop_duplicates(subset=['SKU']), applies .str.title(), exports to Excel, and reports before/after counts. Response B omits two rubric requirements: it does not print column names at all, and only prints row count without showing the column count (incomplete shape). While Response B has a practical advantage in handling column name variations with if/elif checking, it fails the core rubric requirement to print shape and column names immediately.

scenarios.name: parse-ambiguous-dates-and-filter
scenarios.rationale: Response B provides a complete, working solution covering all rubric requirements: pd.to_datetime() with explicit format='%d/%m/%Y', date comparison filtering (dt.year == 2024), and reporting both total rows loaded and matching rows; Response A declines to attempt the task and asks for file location instead, providing no code or implementation of any rubric element.

scenarios.name: multi-metric-aggregation
scenarios.rationale: Response A provides a complete, runnable script that covers all rubric elements (groupby, named aggregations, reset_index, Excel export, row count reporting) plus data inspection and error guidance; Response B shows the correct code structure but is incomplete, hedges with a confirmation request, and crucially omits the required row count reporting.
